text:
MPC gained 0.44% today to close at $414.65, continuing a sharp rebound from last week's lows that has now recovered most of its recent losses. The stock has risen about $42 in five trading days, likely supported by tight refining conditions—US refineries are running at 95.2% capacity while diesel and heating oil inventories sit at just 103.33 million barrels, exactly when heating oil prices have spiked 59% from last winter. Strong refining margins typically help refiners like MPC when product demand is high and inventories are lean.

The broader oil market backdrop has shifted meaningfully. Russian crude production rebounded significantly following geopolitical developments, and the IEA noted that global oil supply has swung back into surplus—meaning crude prices (now $89.62 per barrel domestically) are stabilizing rather than spiking further. That's a relief for refiners' input costs, though the real driver for MPC's week-long rally appears to be the seasonal squeeze in heating oil and diesel supply heading into winter.
